Microsoft has yet to confirm why the services went offline in the early hours of Friday, but it attributes the outage to several servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable after failing automated health checks, which placed elevated strain on the remaining infrastructure worldwide. The Microsoft Service Health Status currently lists all customer services as “operational”, but Microsoft’s update on X indicated there were issues to resolve. Deep Dive “We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they’re not taking as expected. We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances,” said Microsoft 365 Status account on X. Why the services went offline By all accounts, the outage was caused by a cascading infrastructure failure. It began with automated health checks across its server infrastructure, which failed on certain servers and caused them to shut down. This increased the load on the remaining online servers, causing a cascading effect. Microsoft engineers have attempted to restart these servers, and Microsoft 365 Status does indicate that a portion of the affected servers has been restarted and remains stable. Restarting a server requires as long as 30 minutes, depending on hardware and workload. After an unexpected crash or hard reboot, the server may run a disk check process, which can take a long time on large drives. There is no guarantee that the issue which caused the server to shut down or become unresponsive will be fixed by a restart. “We’re testing a configuration change to address a problem that’s causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable,” Microsoft said before it started deploying certain fixes. That attempt hasn’t delivered results so far. Microsoft said the disruption wasn’t driven by a spike in user traffic or a cyberattack. Instead, a core process on affected servers became overwhelmed, causing capacity loss when servers failed automated health checks and dropped offline. As a result, services became unavailable and unstable. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Vishal Mathur Vishal Mathur is Technology Editor for Hindustan Times. news.full_article_text: Man arrested for stabbing nephew for refusing to bring liquor from market in Gurugram The suspect, identified as Raju, is a resident of Chakarpur in Sector-28 and lived with his elder brother and nephew in a rented accommodation. Gurugram police arrested a 35-year-old man for stabbing his nephew with a pair of scissors, leaving him injured after an argument over bringing liquor from the market in Sector-28. The suspect, identified as Raju, is a resident of Chakarpur in Sector-28 and lived with his elder brother and nephew in a rented accommodation. According to the police, he allegedly stabbed his nephew on the head and face around 1.30am on Wednesday after an argument over ordering liquor. What allegedly happened As per police, Raju was addicted to alcohol and was drinking liquor on Tuesday night when he had asked his nephew to fetch him more liquor from the market. Gurugram police's public relations officer (PRO) Sandeep Turan said the victim refused to comply with Raju, resulting in a heated argument. “It was during the argument that Raju picked up a pair of scissors and stabbed his nephew in the head and face,” he said. He said that the victim rushed downstairs in a blood-soaked condition and sought help from Raju’s brother. “The accused fled from the spot after threatening to kill the victim,” the PRO said. FIR filed The suspect's brother immediately alerted the police control room, following which emergency response vehicles reached the spot. On complaint of the suspect’s brother, an FIR was registered against him under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at DLF police station in Sector-29 on Wednesday, after which the suspect was traced and arrested. news.story_lead: 20-year-old undergraduate student dies by suicide at IIT Roorkee Pradeep Singh Bisht, SHO at Roorkee police station, said police received information around midnight that a student had hanged himself in his hostel room. A 20-year-old undergraduate student at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee allegedly died by suicide on Thursday night. The student had been suffering from depression for some time and had visited the institute's wellness centre for over a year.
news.full_article_text: 20-year-old undergraduate student dies by suicide at IIT Roorkee Pradeep Singh Bisht, SHO at Roorkee police station, said police received information around midnight that a student had hanged himself in his hostel room. A 20-year-old undergraduate student at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee allegedly died by suicide on Thursday night. The student had been suffering from depression for some time and had visited the institute's wellness centre for over a year. According to police officials, the student allegedly hanged himself from a ceiling fan using a bedsheet. At around 11 pm, when fellow students knocked on his hostel room door and received no response, they looked through the window and saw him hanging from the ceiling fan. HT reached out to IIT Roorkee media cell in-charge Sonika Srivastava, but she was unavailable for comment. What the police said Pradeep Singh Bisht, station house officer (SHO) at Roorkee police station, said police received information around midnight that a student had hanged himself in his hostel room. "He last met his friends around 3 pm (on Thursday) before returning to his hostel room. When a friend went to check on him at around 11 pm, the door was locked from the inside. Looking through the window, they found him hanging from the ceiling fan with a bedsheet," Bisht said. "Upon receiving the alert around midnight, we reached the spot and brought the body down. He was declared dead following an examination by university doctors," he said. The officer said that the student was undergoing treatment for depression and had been visiting the university's wellness centre for over a year. "We have recovered a suicide note from the spot. He has not blamed anyone for the extreme step, instead citing his depression," he added. "Prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicide. There were no external injuries or signs of struggle on the body. His parents have been informed, and a post-mortem examination will be conducted today," the SHO said. news.story_lead: The Special Investigation Team probing child sex abuse cases involving granite baron R Veeramani has submitted a 720-page charge sheet before a Chennai court, naming five police officers for inaction and evidence suppression. news.full_article_text:
Special Investigation Team Action on Child Sex Abuse Probe

The Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating child sexual abuse allegations against 84-year-old granite baron R Veeramani has submitted a 720-page charge sheet before a local court in Chennai, invoking penal provisions against five police personnel for operational inaction and evidence suppression.

Key Police Officials Named
* Senior officers named include former Greater Chennai Police Commissioner A Arun and Assistant Commissioner MA Yasmin.
* The five officers are charged under Section 21 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act for failing to report or record child sexual abuse offences.
* They are also booked under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Section 199 for public servants disobeying directions of law regarding sexual offence reports, and BNS Section 238 for causing the disappearance of evidence or giving false information to screen offenders.

Case Details and Primary Accused Charges
* The charge sheet is part of one of seven cases registered by the SIT based on complaints from nine minor victims and their mothers.
* The core case was registered on September 27 following a complaint by a mother alleging the abuse of her 14-year-old Scheduled Caste daughter.
* Drivers Parthiban and Babu allegedly transported the victim to Veeramani's Chennai residence.
* Veeramani and his drivers are charged under BNS Section 87 (kidnapping or abducting to force illicit intercourse), BNS Section 351(3) (aggravated criminal intimidation), the POCSO Act, and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
* The 720-page document relies on testimonies from 40 witnesses.

Investigation Chronology and Financial Scrutiny
* October 2025: A pen drive containing video evidence of abuse was handed over to Chennai's Central Crime Branch.
* February 2026: Police submitted a closure report four months after receiving the video, which was subsequently rejected by a local court with instructions to continue probing.
* August 2026: Veeramani and accomplices Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan were arrested.
* October 18, 2026: Manager Shaktivel was arrested for procuring 23 gold bars and transferring cash to influential figures to protect Veeramani.
* Financial probes are scanning the sale of two Chennai properties owned by Veeramani, valued at ₹36.52 crore and ₹43.72 crore, which coincided with the February closure report, to check for official bribery.
* The SIT has issued five lookout circulars, including for Veeramani's daughter Archana and businessman Prakash. Proceedings are underway to impound the passport and extradite Prakash, currently absconding in the United Kingdom, for facilitating financial transfers to police personnel.

hindi_translation.headline: एसआईटी ने बाल यौन शोषण मामले में निष्क्रियता के लिए ग्रेटर चेन्नई के पूर्व शीर्ष पुलिस अधिकारी और चार अन्य पर आरोप पत्र दाखिल किया
hindi_translation.story_lead: ग्रेनाइट कारोबारी आर वीरामणि से जुड़े बाल यौन शोषण मामले की जांच कर रही विशेष जांच टीम (SIT) ने एक स्थानीय अदालत में 720 पन्नों का आरोप पत्र दाखिल किया है, जिसमें पूर्व ग्रेटर चेन्नई पुलिस आयुक्त ए अरुण और सहायक आयुक्त एमए यास्मीन सहित पांच पुलिस अधिकारियों को निष्क्रियता और साक्ष्य छिपाने का आरोपी बनाया गया है। इन अधिकारियों पर पॉक्सो अधिनियम और भारतीय न्याय संहिता के तहत अक्टूबर 2025 में सौंपी गई डिजिटल साक्ष्यों पर कार्रवाई न करने और मामले को दबाने का प्रयास करने के आरोप लगाए गए हैं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
बाल यौन उत्पीड़न मामले की एसआईटी जांच पर कार्रवाई

84 वर्षीय ग्रेनाइट कारोबारी आर वीरामणि से जुड़े बाल यौन शोषण के मामलों की जांच कर रही विशेष जांच टीम (एसआईटी) ने चेन्नई की एक अदालत में 720 पन्नों का आरोप पत्र प्रस्तुत किया है, जिसमें पांच पुलिस कर्मियों को प्रक्रियात्मक निष्क्रियता और साक्ष्य गायब करने के लिए नामित किया गया है।

नामित मुख्य पुलिस अधिकारी
* नामित वरिष्ठ अधिकारियों में ग्रेटर चेन्नई के पूर्व पुलिस आयुक्त ए अरुण और सहायक आयुक्त एमए यास्मीन शामिल हैं।
* इन पांच अधिकारियों पर बच्चों को यौन अपराधों से संरक्षण (POCSO) अधिनियम की धारा 21 के तहत बाल यौन शोषण की रिपोर्ट न करने या दर्ज न करने का आरोप है।
* उनके खिलाफ भारतीय न्याय संहिता (BNS) की धारा 199 (यौन अपराधों की रिपोर्ट दर्ज करने से संबंधित कानूनी निर्देशों की अवहेलना) और धारा 238 (अपराध के साक्ष्य गायब करना या झूठी जानकारी देना) के तहत भी मामले दर्ज किए गए हैं।

मुख्य मामले के विवरण और मुख्य आरोपी पर आरोप
* यह आरोप पत्र नौ नाबालिग पीड़ितों और उनकी माताओं की शिकायतों पर एसआईटी द्वारा दर्ज सात मामलों में से एक में दाखिल किया गया है।
* मुख्य मामला 27 सितंबर को एक मां की शिकायत पर दर्ज किया गया था, जिसमें आरोप लगाया गया था कि उसकी 14 वर्षीय अनुसूचित जाति की बेटी का यौन उत्पीड़न किया गया।
* ड्राइवर पार्थिबन और बाबू कथित तौर पर पीड़िता को वीरामणि के चेन्नई स्थित आवास पर ले गए थे।
* वीरामणि और उनके ड्राइवरों पर बीएनएस धारा 87 (अपहरण या अवैध संबंध के लिए मजबूर करना), बीएनएस धारा 351(3) (गंभीर आपराधिक धमकी), पॉक्सो अधिनियम और अनुसूचित जाति एवं अनुसूचित जनजाति (अत्याचार निवारण) अधिनियम के तहत आरोप लगाए गए हैं।
* यह 720 पन्नों का आरोप पत्र 40 गवाहों के बयानों पर आधारित है।

जांच का क्रमबद्ध विवरण और वित्तीय जांच
* अक्टूबर 2025: यौन उत्पीड़न का वीडियो वाला पेन ड्राइव चेन्नई की सेंट्रल क्राइम ब्रांच को सौंपा गया।
* फरवरी 2026: वीडियो प्राप्त करने के चार महीने बाद पुलिस ने क्लोजर रिपोर्ट दाखिल की, जिसे स्थानीय अदालत ने खारिज कर दिया और जांच जारी रखने के निर्देश दिए।
* अगस्त 2026: वीरामणि और उनके सहयोगियों शांति और महेंद्र सिम्हन को गिरफ्तार किया गया।
* 18 अक्टूबर, 2026: प्रबंधक शक्तिवेल को 23 सोने की छड़ें खरीदने और प्रभावशाली लोगों को नकद हस्तांतरित करने के आरोप में गिरफ्तार किया गया।
* वित्तीय जांच में चेन्नई के पास स्थित वीरामणि की दो संपत्तियों की बिक्री (₹36.52 करोड़ और ₹43.72 करोड़) की जांच की जा रही है, जो फरवरी की क्लोजर रिपोर्ट के समय हुई थी, ताकि रिश्वतखोरी की संभावना का पता लगाया जा सके।
* एसआईटी ने वीरामणि की बेटी अर्चना और व्यवसायी प्रकाश सहित पांच लोगों के खिलाफ लुकआउट सर्कुलर जारी किए हैं। ब्रिटेन में छिपे भगोड़े प्रकाश का पासपोर्ट जब्त करने और प्रत्यर्पण की कार्यवाही शुरू की गई है।

news.full_article_text: IIT Kharagpur becomes first IIT to offer MD programmes approved by national medical body IIT Kharagpur become the first IIT to offer postgraduate medical courses recognised by NMC, introducing 12 MD seats across six specialisations. Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur in West Bengal has become the first IIT in India to introduce postgraduate medical degree programmes recognised by the National Medical Commission (NMC), offering 12 MD seats across six specialisations for the 2026-27 academic session, the institute announced on Thursday. “The Institute undertook the prescribed regulatory process with the NMC, including submission of applications, documentation of academic and clinical facilities, and fulfilment of the applicable requirements in March 2026. The process culminated in permission for the six MD programmes for the academic session 2026–27,” director of IIT Kharagpur Suman Chakraborty said. The programmes will be offered at the institute’s Dr B C Roy Multi-Speciality Medical Research Centre, with admissions through the second round of NEET-PG 2026 counselling from November 10 to 23, according to the announcement. Fees of the PG medical course and stipends paid to students will be on the lines of AIIMS. “The postgraduate medical programmes are supported by the in-house expanding clinical infrastructure of Dr. Shyama Prasad Mookerji Superspeciality Hospital - new Hospital of IIT Kharagpur, together with the South Eastern Railway Hospital, Kharagpur, under the established institutional partnership. This arrangement provides the clinical training ecosystem for the approved postgraduate programmes, in accordance with the applicable NMC requirements,” Chakraborty said. The six specialisations are general medicine, radiology, physiology, pathology, community medicine and biochemistry, with two seats in each discipline. The programmes will be available for eligible candidates through the Medical Counselling Committee’s (MCC) online counselling process. MCC is the government body responsible for conducting online counselling to allot medical and dental seats based on NEET scores. The move marks the entry of an IIT into postgraduate medical education and is aimed at bringing clinical medicine closer to engineering, artificial intelligence (AI), biomedical sciences and translational research. IIT Kharagpur said in a statement that the programmes would provide opportunities for medical students to engage with research across areas such as AI-assisted clinical decision-making, advanced medical imaging, computational pathology, biomedical devices, molecular diagnostics, precision medicine and population health. The institute added that its existing strengths in microfluidics, bioengineering, healthcare diagnostics, AI, computational sciences and translational medical technologies would provide a foundation for the interdisciplinary approach. Chakraborty said the institute’s objective was not limited to training specialist doctors but also included developing medical professionals capable of addressing healthcare challenges through research and technology. “India’s first IIT is now taking a historic step towards shaping the future of medical education. Our vision is not simply to train specialist doctors, but to create an ecosystem where clinical excellence meets engineering ingenuity, artificial intelligence and translational research,” he said. “We want our medical graduates to be not only outstanding clinicians, but also innovators capable of addressing some of humanity’s most pressing healthcare challenges,” Chakraborty added. He said the first batch would be pioneers of a new academic journey, with the institute aiming to nurture doctors who can combine clinical understanding with scientific discovery and technological innovation. Established in 1951, IIT Kharagpur was the first institute in the IIT system. Its entry into postgraduate medical education comes in its 75th year and is part of its broader ambition to expand the role of technological institutions in addressing healthcare challenges. The institute also said that it has identified research-driven learning and international academic exposure as elements of the proposed academic environment. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sanjay Maurya Sanjay Maurya is a Principal Correspondent with Hindustan Times, where he covers education, with a focus on school and higher education, competitive examinations, education policy and governance. news.headline: Was Delhi pollution data during Diwali misleading?
news.story_lead: - Published 12 November 2026, 09:01 GMT BBC Verify has found significant discrepancies between two Indian government datasets showing Delhi's air pollution during Diwali, indicating official figures may not have captured the full extent of the problem. As fireworks lit up Delhi's skies on 8 November to mark one of India's biggest festivals, some monitoring stations recorded very high levels of PM2.5, a fine particulate matter which can damage people's lungs and cause other serious health problems. But every hourly PM2.5 reading above 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre was excluded from the widely cited air quality index (AQI) published by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), even though these higher readings were present in the data from the Delhi Pollution Control Commission (DPCC).
news.full_article_text: - Published 12 November 2026, 09:01 GMT BBC Verify has found significant discrepancies between two Indian government datasets showing Delhi's air pollution during Diwali, indicating official figures may not have captured the full extent of the problem. As fireworks lit up Delhi's skies on 8 November to mark one of India's biggest festivals, some monitoring stations recorded very high levels of PM2.5, a fine particulate matter which can damage people's lungs and cause other serious health problems. But every hourly PM2.5 reading above 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre was excluded from the widely cited air quality index (AQI) published by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), even though these higher readings were present in the data from the Delhi Pollution Control Commission (DPCC). Delhi is one of the most polluted cities in the world and often has dangerously poor air quality , so it is vital people living in India's capital can trust the official data. Firecrackers are not the only cause of pollution, which is also attributed to a mix of reasons including vehicle emissions, construction dust, farm fires and atmospheric factors. But they can worsen air quality, especially in winter. Government critics and opposition parties have accused the government of deliberately under-reporting the pollution data. The CPCB rejected this in a statement, which said the body was "committed to transparent, scientific and reliable reporting". The CPCB, whose figures are generally cited by Indian media, said readings above 1,000 micrograms are treated as "outside" the range for detection its equipment has been calibrated for and are excluded from calculations. "During extreme episodes which are occasional like Diwali firecracker bursting, this may appear as a data gap at the particular station concerned, and those hours do not contribute to the 24-hour average of relevant pollutant for concerned station," the statement added. Dr Manoj Kumar, a researcher at Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), told BBC Verify that excluding high readings risks misrepresenting actual pollution levels and could cause people to lose trust in official figures. Our analysis found that, across the same 30 stations over 24 hours covering Diwali night, available CPCB readings averaged 240 micrograms per cubic metre - less than half the average of 551 in DPCC's data. What does the pollution data show? On the night of Diwali from Sunday into Monday, Delhi's already high pollution levels rose sharply as the celebrations peaked. Three different pollution monitoring stations recorded PM2.5 hourly concentrations above 3,000 micrograms, DPCC data examined by BBC Verify shows. Dr Kumar said that even a short-term exposure to extreme levels of particulate matter can have adverse health impacts. The World Health Organization's air quality guidelines state that annual average concentrations should not exceed five micrograms per cubic metre. Between 21:00 local time (15:30 GMT) on 8 November and 07:00 on 9 November, during the peak of Diwali celebrations, 217 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 16 stations reported complete data during this period, while 43 had at least one missing observation. None of the 116 readings above 1,000 micrograms from the 30 DPCC-managed stations appeared in the CPCB's published records they feed data into. This matters because stations need at least 16 hours of valid PM2.5 measurements to calculate a daily average, according to CPCB's methodology. So a station with too many missing or invalid readings will not contribute to official pollution calculations. One example of a station with several hours of missing data was at RK Puram in south Delhi, where pollution peaked at nearly 2,500 micrograms. Using hourly PM2.5 readings from this station, BBC Verify calculated an average concentration of about 945 micrograms over the 24-hour period after 17:00 on 8 November. But similar averages of CPCB's published data for 14 of those 24 hours produced a much lower figure of 299 micrograms. The missing 10 hours also meant this data was not included in daily average calculations. The missing data across the city means that, despite a sharp overnight rise in pollution at some monitoring stations, CPCB reported Delhi's AQI at 344 at 16:00 on 9 November, down from 376 at the same time the day before. Dr Sierra Clark, an environmental epidemiologist from City St George's, University in London, warned classifying high pollution readings as missing could leave out days which "contribute the most to short-term health events, such as asthma attacks and heart attacks". She told BBC Verify "for transparency", Delhi's pollution reporting could show two scenarios including and excluding extreme pollution episodes. "The latter would give a sense of typical pollution levels that are more representative of people's day-to-day experience. But it is also important to show the impact of those few days and what they contribute," Dr Clark added. Pollution in Delhi is not limited to PM2.5 and satellite imagery shows a thick haze over the city on 8 and 9 November. Satellite measurements of other pollutants like nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO) and fire activity in the atmosphere, rather than at ground level, showed increases on 8 November. But their overall average for Diwali week was not very high compared with 2024 and 2025. Graphics by Jess Carr and Tom Shiel. What do you want BBC Verify to investigate? news.headline: Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard who reprimanded him and group
news.story_lead: US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery. - Published 11 November 2026 US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery. A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet.
news.full_article_text: US Army guard reprimands group that includes US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery. - Published 11 November 2026 US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery. A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet. In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier". Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias. He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads. In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times." Hegseth (right) awarded the medal to Specialist Thomas Iglesias after being reprimanded by him The Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct. The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell later said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum." "The Secretary and the entire Department have always honoured - and will always honour - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe." A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948. It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and First Lady Melania Trump bow their heads in prayer during a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery. During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war. "Under this administration, and it was about time, somebody fought back. All of us fought back," he said. "And we won," Trump said of the Iran war. "It's just a question of when we want to end it. We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory." Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary. Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth amid Democratic lawmakers' push to impeach him. On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill . Hegseth has called the impeachment efforts a "farce" and a "stunt". news.headline: Suspected bomb hoax threats force fresh evacuations of Italian schools
news.story_lead: Bomb squads have searched many schools but no devices have been found - Published 12 November 2026, 12:39 GMT Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations. Some 3,778 schools, from Milan in the north to Sicily in the south, reported similar threats to one that created chaos on Wednesday - even though no explosive devices have been found. The government has advised schools that "in the absence of concrete evidence beyond the simple receipt of a mass email indicating a danger, buildings must not not be evacuated".
news.full_article_text: Bomb squads have searched many schools but no devices have been found - Published 12 November 2026, 12:39 GMT Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations. Some 3,778 schools, from Milan in the north to Sicily in the south, reported similar threats to one that created chaos on Wednesday - even though no explosive devices have been found. The government has advised schools that "in the absence of concrete evidence beyond the simple receipt of a mass email indicating a danger, buildings must not not be evacuated". Unlike a day earlier, only 77 schools were evacuated on Thursday, authorities say. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says her government will come up with "sector-specific" advice to help those facing this kind of threat. Schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland received threats on Wednesday, too. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected. On Thursday morning, a bomb alert at a Calais rail station delayed international and national train services in northern France. The latest incidents follow a series of bomb hoaxes last week against airports and airlines in a number of European countries. Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings. Wednesday's email threat - sent to 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 Italian state schools - was said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan". Some officials say it originated in Taiwan. A similar message sent to Italian schools on Thursday, again signed by Mikhail Andropov, is said to have been sent from the account of a teacher in the Philippines whose account is believed to have been hacked. - No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister Published 1 day ago - Police treating threatening email sent to more than 300 schools as 'hoax' Published 1 day ago Many parents, though, are concerned and have been demanding clarity and action from the government. La Repubblica newspaper reports that protests have been held against a decision by the headmaster of a secondary school in Rome who did not take any action, saying she had realised the threatening message to contain typos and therefore be "fake". According to the newspaper, protesters want new national guidelines to be issued. Related topics More on this story - Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats Published 6 days ago

news.headline: Union Government's Protracted Disputes Over Foreign Arbitral Awards Test India's Credibility
news.story_lead: Repeated legal challenges by the Union government against foreign arbitral awards are raising concerns regarding India's reputation as a reliable destination for international business and arbitration. The prolonged litigation highlights structural challenges in enforcing international commercial decisions within India's legal framework.
news.full_article_text:
### Challenges in Enforcing Foreign Arbitral Awards

Reports highlighted by the Supreme Court Observer draw attention to the Union of India's extended litigation against adverse foreign arbitral awards, examining how such prolonged legal contests affect the nation's international standing.

#### Key Concerns Highlighted
- **Impact on Global Credibility:** Continuous state challenges against adverse awards handed down by international tribunals raise doubts among global investors about contractual enforcement in India.
- **Commercial Legal Uncertainty:** Extended legal disputes increase litigation costs and create uncertainties for international commercial partners.
- **Arbitration Ambitions vs Reality:** While India seeks to position itself as a global commercial arbitration hub, routine challenges to international arbitral awards run counter to standard international practices.
bullet_points: The Union government's ongoing legal battles against foreign arbitral awards test India's global credibility.
Protracted litigation over international arbitration decisions creates uncertainty for foreign commercial partners.
Enforcement of foreign arbitral awards is a critical metric for international business confidence and ease of doing business.
The situation underscores tensions between state litigation practices and national ambitions to become an international arbitration hub.
key_facts: The Supreme Court Observer reported on the impact of government litigation over foreign arbitral awards on India's credibility.
Foreign arbitral enforcement directly affects international commercial relations and investor perception.
important_dates: 2026-11-12: Publication of the report assessing the impact of foreign arbitral award litigation on India's credibility.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Legal provisions under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and international conventions like the New York Convention.
Mains: GS Paper III (Ease of Doing Business, Investment Models) and GS Paper II (Dispute resolution mechanisms and statutory governance).
news.upsc_analysis: The state's practice of challenging foreign arbitral awards highlights the broader challenge of contract enforcement in India. For India to establish itself as a foreign investment destination and international arbitration hub, consistent execution of arbitral awards with minimal judicial interference is vital.
causes: Government resistance to adverse financial or contractual outcomes from international arbitration bodies.
impacts: Deterrence of international business confidence and potential impacts on foreign direct investment flows.
Questions regarding India's commitment to international arbitration standards.
challenges: Balancing domestic public policy considerations with international treaty commitments.
Reducing delays in deciding validity challenges against foreign arbitral awards.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (Part II: Enforcement of Certain Foreign Awards).
Article 253 of the Constitution of India regarding laws for giving effect to international agreements.
way_forward: Adopt a more restrained litigation policy by state entities regarding foreign arbitral awards.
Strengthen specialized commercial courts to handle foreign award enforcement rapidly.
news.mains_notes: Enforcing foreign arbitral awards is essential for maintaining investor confidence and contract sanctity in international commercial trade. Routine appeals by state actors weaken India's positioning as an international arbitration destination.
mains_questions: Analyze how prolonged challenges by government entities against foreign arbitral awards impact India's efforts to improve its Ease of Doing Business framework.
Discuss the statutory framework governing the enforcement of foreign arbitral awards in India under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
news.takeaway: Prolonged legal challenges by the government against foreign arbitral awards risk compromising India's standing as an investor-friendly and arbitration-oriented jurisdiction.
prelims_facts: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 governs foreign arbitral award recognition under Part II.
The New York Convention (1958) facilitates recognition of foreign arbitral decisions across signatory nations.

hindi_translation.headline: विदेशी मध्यस्थता निर्णयों पर केंद्र सरकार की लंबी कानूनी लड़ाई से भारत की विश्वसनीयता पर सवाल
hindi_translation.story_lead: विदेशी मध्यस्थता (आर्बिट्रेशन) निर्णयों के खिलाफ केंद्र सरकार की लंबी कानूनी चुनौतियां अंतरराष्ट्रीय व्यापार और मध्यस्थता केंद्र के रूप में भारत की साख पर चिंताएं पैदा कर रही हैं। यह लंबी मुकदमेबाजी भारत के कानूनी ढांचे के भीतर अंतरराष्ट्रीय वाणिज्यिक निर्णयों को लागू करने की चुनौतियों को रेखांकित करती है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### विदेशी मध्यस्थता निर्णयों को लागू करने की चुनौतियां

सुप्रीम कोर्ट ऑब्जर्वर द्वारा उजागर की गई रिपोर्टों में प्रतिकूल विदेशी मध्यस्थता निर्णयों के खिलाफ भारत सरकार की लंबी मुकदमों पर ध्यान आकर्षित किया गया है, जिसमें यह विश्लेषण किया गया है कि ऐसी कानूनी चुनौतियां देश की अंतरराष्ट्रीय साख को कैसे प्रभावित करती हैं।

#### मुख्य चिंताएं
- **वैश्विक विश्वसनीयता पर प्रभाव:** अंतरराष्ट्रीय न्यायाधिकरणों के फैसलों के खिलाफ लगातार सरकारी चुनौतियों से वैश्विक निवेशकों के बीच भारत में अनुबंध प्रवर्तन को लेकर संदेह उत्पन्न होता है।
- **वाणिज्यिक कानूनी अनिश्चितता:** लंबी कानूनी लड़ाइयों से मुकदमेबाजी की लागत बढ़ती है और अंतरराष्ट्रीय वाणिज्यिक साझेदारों के लिए अनिश्चितता पैदा होती है।
- **मध्यस्थता की आकांक्षाएं बनाम वास्तविकता:** भारत खुद को एक वैश्विक वाणिज्यिक मध्यस्थता हब के रूप में स्थापित करना चाहता है, लेकिन विदेशी निर्णयों को नियमित रूप से चुनौती देना इस अंतरराष्ट्रीय लक्ष्य के विपरीत है।
bullet_points: विदेशी मध्यस्थता फैसलों के खिलाफ केंद्र सरकार की जारी कानूनी लड़ाई भारत की वैश्विक विश्वसनीयता का परीक्षण करती है।
अंतरराष्ट्रीय मध्यस्थता निर्णयों पर लंबी मुकदमेबाजी विदेशी वाणिज्यिक साझेदारों के लिए अनिश्चितता पैदा करती है।
विदेशी मध्यस्थता निर्णयों का प्रवर्तन अंतरराष्ट्रीय व्यापार विश्वास के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण कारक है।
यह स्थिति सरकारी मुकदमेबाजी प्रथाओं और भारत को अंतरराष्ट्रीय मध्यस्थता केंद्र बनाने की आकांक्षाओं के बीच तनाव को दर्शाती है।
key_facts: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ऑब्जर्वर ने भारत की विश्वसनीयता पर विदेशी मध्यस्थता फैसलों पर सरकारी मुकदमेबाजी के प्रभाव पर रिपोर्ट जारी की।
विदेशी मध्यस्थता प्रवर्तन सीधे तौर पर अंतरराष्ट्रीय वाणिज्यिक संबंधों को प्रभावित करता है।

### National Naturopathy Day: Significance and Health Framework

National Naturopathy Day serves as an annual national observance aimed at promoting drugless systems of healing and wellness across India. Governed under the broader mandate of the Ministry of AYUSH, the day stresses the importance of non-invasive, nature-based medical systems, preventive health interventions, and lifestyle medicine.

Key aspects associated with the observance include:
- **Focus on Research:** Encouraging clinical research and evidence-based validation of traditional naturopathic treatments and wellness therapies.
- **Preventive Healthcare:** Advocating for lifestyle modifications, natural nutrition, and stress management as primary mechanisms for disease prevention.
- **Holistic Integration:** Aligning traditional drugless therapies with modern wellness paradigms to strengthen public health outcomes.

hindi_translation.story_lead: राष्ट्रीय प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा दिवस का उद्देश्य बिना दवा, निवारक और समग्र स्वास्थ्य देखभाल प्रणालियों के बारे में जागरूकता बढ़ाना है। यह दिन स्वस्थ जीवन शैली के विकल्पों को बढ़ावा देने के लिए पारंपरिक प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा पद्धतियों के साथ वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान के एकीकरण पर जोर देता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### राष्ट्रीय प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा दिवस: महत्व और स्वास्थ्य ढांचा

राष्ट्रीय प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा दिवस पूरे भारत में प्राकृतिक और बिना दवा वाली स्वास्थ्य प्रणालियों को बढ़ावा देने के उद्देश्य से मनाया जाता है। आयुष मंत्रालय के व्यापक जनादेश के तहत संचालित, यह दिन गैर-आक्रामक, प्रकृति-आधारित चिकित्सा प्रणालियों, निवारक स्वास्थ्य हस्तक्षेपों और जीवन शैली चिकित्सा के महत्व पर बल देता है।

इस आयोजन से जुड़े प्रमुख पहलू:
- **अनुसंधान पर ध्यान:** पारंपरिक प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा और वेलनेस थेरेपी के नैदानिक अनुसंधान और साक्ष्य-आधारित सत्यापन को प्रोत्साहित करना।
- **निवारक स्वास्थ्य देखभाल:** बीमारी की रोकथाम के प्राथमिक तरीकों के रूप में जीवन शैली में बदलाव, प्राकृतिक पोषण और तनाव प्रबंधन की वकालत करना।
- **समग्र एकीकरण:** सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य परिणामों को मजबूत करने के लिए आधुनिक वेलनेस मापदंडों के साथ पारंपरिक दवाओं का समन्वय करना।
bullet_points: राष्ट्रीय प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा दिवस बिना दवा और गैर-आक्रामक स्वास्थ्य प्रणालियों पर जोर देता है।
इस दिन का उद्देश्य प्राकृतिक चिकित्सा तकनीकों और निवारक चिकित्सा के बारे में जागरूकता बढ़ाना है।
यह वैकल्पिक स्वास्थ्य और कल्याण पद्धतियों में साक्ष्य-आधारित नैदानिक अनुसंधान को बढ़ावा देता है।
